description: The hand-verified expected result for the negative Trivy native fixture that carries one Vulnerabilities[] record from which no package coordinate can be formed at any of the four precedence levels. Every value was derived by reading the fixture and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/, never by running the adapter and recording what it printed. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/trivy.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match. The structure follows expected/reject-sarif-unresolvable-path.rows.json, which is this folder's declared template for a negative expected file: three parts, in order -- the documentation and metadata that fix the contract, then rows with row_derivations, then rejections with what the fixture does not reach. Every key that file uses is reused here with the same meaning, and every key the positive sibling expected/derived-trivy-features.rows.json adds for this tool -- scanner_class_by_section, scanner_class_falsifiability, aap_reported_counters, prohibitions_observed, discrepancies_recorded, how_to_check_this_file -- is reused with its meaning too, so one generic loader reads both.
scanner_class: per record -- vuln, secret or misconfig -- taken from the section array the record was read from. Trivy is the one tool in AAP 0.5.4's class table whose scanner_class is not fixed, and the rejection this file asserts is the one condition that is section-dependent for the same reason: only a Vulnerabilities record is dependency-oriented, so only a Vulnerabilities record can earn it.
scanner_class_derivation: The enclosing section array decides the class and nothing else does. adapters/trivy.py fixes the mapping once in SUPPORTED_SECTIONS, resolves it through scanner_class_for_section(section), and hands the section name to adapt_record as a required argument; no branch of that function consults a record's own fields, and a section outside those three yields an unattributable_section rejection rather than a class. Every scanner_class below is therefore checkable by re-walking the fixture and reading which array the record sits in.

scanner_class_falsifiability.why_the_content_misleads: Every piece of prose on this record points at the secret scanner. Its Title is "Secrets passed via `build-args` or envs or copied secret files", its Message is "Possible exposure of secret env \"SPARK_HOME\" in ENV", its Resolution talks about secret mounts, and its Namespace is builtin.dockerfile.DS031. Any implementation that keyed the class off record content would class this row secret.
scanner_class_falsifiability.why_misconfig_is_correct: It is an element of Results[0].Misconfigurations[], and the section array is the sole source of the class. SUPPORTED_SECTIONS maps Misconfigurations to misconfig, so this row is misconfig.
scanner_class_falsifiability.what_this_row_falsifies: The section-not-content derivation. An implementation reading record content would emit secret here and still satisfy every other assertion in this file. If this row ever reads secret, the derivation has been inverted; that is a defect to diagnose, not a value to update.
scanner_class_falsifiability.why_it_matters_to_this_fixture_in_partic: The class decides whether a record is dependency-oriented, and dependency-orientation decides whether an absent package coordinate is a rejection or an ordinary null. So an inverted derivation would not merely mislabel this row -- it would move the rejection to the wrong record. A content sniff that read /Results/0/Misconfigurations/0 as a package finding would look for a coordinate it has none of and reject it, while the genuinely defective record at /Results/4/Vulnerabilities/0 became a row with a null coordinate. Both counts would still reconcile.
scanner_class_falsifiability.corollary: The same rule runs the other way on row 2, whose RuleID is jwt-token: it is a secret because it sits in Secrets[], not because its identifier names a token format.

fixture.derivation: A negative fixture is derived from its positive sibling rather than being an excerpt of it, so the provenance is stated as a derivation and the derivation is stated exactly. Against fixtures/derived-trivy-features.json (sha256 baa20547c89c73bcffaacb33924da2a6ea9782db4c1b0840a50b6cb6cc648313, 12226 bytes, 343 lines) a diff reports three edits, all of them inside /Results/4 and none of them anywhere else: Target changes from "Node.js" to "core/src/main/resources/org/apache/spark/ui/static/package.json"; Type changes from "node-pkg" to "npm"; and PkgID, PkgName, PkgIdentifier, PkgPath, InstalledVersion, FixedVersion and Status are removed from /Results/4/Vulnerabilities/0. Eight of the nine records are byte-identical to the positive fixture's, which is what makes the one defective record the only difference this file's assertions can be about. Throughout this file, "the positive fixture" and "the positive sibling" name the declared-derived document this fixture is derived from -- oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/derived-trivy-features.json and its expected file oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/expected/derived-trivy-features.rows.json, whose nine finding records and nine rows are the ones cited by index below. Neither term names oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/trivy.json, which is a byte-for-byte copy of harness/artifacts/raw/trivy.json carrying only its three DS-0026 misconfiguration records, nor that file's expected file expected/trivy.rows.json.
fixture.what_the_derivation_buys: Two things a fresh fixture could not. First, the eight surviving rows below are the same eight the positive sibling already hand-verified from the same bytes, so a disagreement between the two files is itself a detectable fault rather than two independent guesses. Second, the record that changed is the one the positive sibling used to demonstrate the per-record path refinement -- its PkgPath refined a Target of "Node.js" -- so removing the package fields and promoting the manifest to the Target leaves a record whose path resolves perfectly well and whose only defect is the coordinate. That isolation is the whole point: a record defective in two ways at once would be counted under whichever condition the classification order reaches first, and would prove nothing about the second.
fixture.defective_record_is_in_vulnerabilities: Required, not incidental. adapters/trivy.py's _DEPENDENCY_ORIENTED_SECTIONS is frozenset({"Vulnerabilities"}), so a record with no formable coordinate in Secrets[] or Misconfigurations[] becomes a row with a null coordinate and could never produce this rejection. Putting the defective record anywhere else would make the fixture assert the opposite of what it exists to assert.
fixture.fixture_is_never_edited_to_suit_these_ro: These rows are re-derived when the fixture changes, which is what the recorded sha256, byte count and line count above make visible. The fixture is the input and this file is the assertion; the dependency runs one way.

routing.detected_by: normalize.shape -- the document carries no version of "2.1.0" and no runs array, so it is not SARIF, and it routes to the native adapter keyed by the runner that wrote it
routing.routing_decision: normalize.shape.route("trivy", doc) returns tool "trivy", shape "trivy", adapter "trivy"; scanner_class is per record for this tool and is therefore not fixed by the route
routing.not_a_shape_failure: No normalize.shape.UnknownArtifactShape is expected here, and a test asserting one against this fixture would be asserting the wrong thing. The enclosing document is a well-formed Trivy 0.74.0 filesystem report and routes cleanly; exactly one record inside it is defective, and the adapter rejects that record while still emitting the other eight. The fixtures that own shape-detection failure are near-sarif-version-only.json, near-sarif-runs-only.json and unknown-shape.json.
routing.not_a_halt: No trivy.UnsupportedTrivySection is expected either. Licenses and ExperimentalModifiedFindings are present and empty on all six Results[] elements, so validate_finding_sections returns None. That matters more here than in the positive sibling: a halt raises before a single row is built, so a non-empty unsupported section would pre-empt the rejection entirely and this fixture would assert nothing. The halt's own fixture is halt-trivy-unsupported-section.json.
routing.negative_routing_test: The mandated negative routing assertion -- that a native artifact must not route to the SARIF adapter -- belongs to test_shape_routing_negative.py. This fixture is a native artifact and is eligible for it, but the assertion is that file's, not this one's.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent -- exactly emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS.
package_coordinate_is_permitted_absent_a: The conditional this fixture exists to keep from being flattened, and it is not a contradiction. package_coordinate is a member of emit.OPTIONAL_FIELDS, so a row may carry null there and be written without complaint -- and four rows below do. What makes the ninth record a rejection is not the schema but the section: adapters/trivy.py applies the absence test only to a record from _DEPENDENCY_ORIENTED_SECTIONS, because a vulnerability is a finding about a package and a finding about a package that names no package cannot be attributed with certainty. A secret and a misconfiguration are findings about a file, so absence there is ordinary. One field, two meanings, decided by the enclosing array and by nothing else.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations.

resolution_context.root_independence: Every Target in this fixture is already root-relative and the recorded path base for trivy is the scan root itself, so joining onto the base and relativizing back to the root returns the reported string unchanged. No record here carries a per-record path refinement at all. These rows therefore hold for whatever absolute scan root the adapter is given, and no absolute path appears anywhere in this file.
resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the trivy entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.why_the_merged_artifact_is_root_relative: The runner invokes trivy fs once per scope directory, because that subcommand takes exactly one path, and its merge step prefixes every part's Target with that part's own ArtifactName and sets the merged ArtifactName to ".". The metadata records that, which is why the base is the scan root rather than any one directory.
resolution_context.path_base_caveat: That base holds for the merged artifact only. The same metadata records that the eighteen retained per-directory reports under logs/trivy.parts/ are not root-anchored and must be read with per_section_target semantics and an explicit section_base. This fixture is the merged shape, so section_base is null and passing one would be wrong rather than harmless.
resolution_context.target_is_the_base: path comes from the enclosing Results[].Target, refined by a per-record path where the section supplies one. Only Vulnerabilities declares such a field -- PkgPath -- and no record in this fixture carries it, so every path here is its Target unrefined. paths.resolve_trivy_path owns every base decision; the adapter relativizes, joins and strips nothing itself.
resolution_context.per_record_refinement_in_this_fixture: None. per_record_path_refinements is 0, where the positive sibling records 1: the PkgPath that produced that refinement is one of the members this fixture's derivation removes. The path it used to refine to is now the Target itself, so the resolved path is the same string by a different route -- which is worth stating, because a reader comparing the two files would otherwise see a counter drop with no visible cause.
resolution_context.path_kind: tree_file on all eight rows: no path carries an ! and none begins with a .. segment, so non_filesystem_paths is 0 and no row is excluded from scope on kind alone. The rejected record's Target is a tree file too, and it still contributes to no path_kind counter, because those are counted only for a record that becomes a row.
resolution_context.severity_source: Every one of the eight emitted records states a Severity label that is in severity.py's mapped vocabulary, so the label governs on all eight and no CVSS score is consulted on any of them -- AAP 0.5.4's precedence, visible here as severity_basis label on every row while three of them do carry a CVSS table. severity_native keeps the literal exactly as the artifact wrote it, in upper case, and severity_norm is the band that literal maps to.
resolution_context.severity_mapping_exercised: CRITICAL to Critical, HIGH to High, MEDIUM to Medium, and UNKNOWN to Info. LOW to Low is not exercised by any row: the only LOW record in the fixture is the rejected one, and a rejected record is never fed to the severity resolver or to the tally, so no Low band and no LOW literal appears below. That is a real consequence of the rejection and it is recorded rather than smoothed over.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: Three states appear across the nine records. Two of the four precedence levels supply a value: the record's own PkgIdentifier.PURL on two rows, a PURL on the matching enclosing Packages[] entry on one, and the ecosystem coordinate <lower-cased Results[].Type>:<PkgName>@<InstalledVersion> on one. The field is null on the four secret and misconfiguration rows, where absence is ordinary. And on the ninth record no level can form anything at all, which -- because that record is dependency-oriented -- is the rejection.

why_this_case_is_realistic.claim: A Trivy vulnerability record that resolves to no package is a normal outcome against this scanned tree, not a contrived one.
why_this_case_is_realistic.grounding: Exactly one manifest-shaped file is in scope across the whole twelve-glob expansion: core/src/main/resources/org/apache/spark/ui/static/package.json. Verified in the pinned clone at 59b8a4489c878fa3a9aa6b7fbae760f2fc80eb9d -- 5 lines, 80 bytes, carrying a name, a license and "type": "module", with no dependencies block and no lockfile beside it.
why_this_case_is_realistic.why_that_makes_the_case_ordinary: That file is the Target of the defective record, and it is the only in-scope file a vulnerability record could plausibly be attributed to. A manifest with no dependencies block declares no package, so a scanner that reaches it and still emits a vulnerability record has nothing to name as the package -- no PURL to copy, no PkgName and no InstalledVersion to render a coordinate from, and no Packages inventory beside it to fall back on. The eighteen scope directories hold no pom.xml, no requirements*.txt, no setup.py, no pyproject.toml and no JAR, so there is no second manifest to make this an outlier against.
why_this_case_is_realistic.why_it_is_stated_here: A negative fixture that only ever exercises an impossible shape teaches a reader to treat the rejection as theoretical, and a rejection treated as theoretical is one nobody checks. This one names a real file, at a real commit, with a real reason for carrying no package.
why_this_case_is_realistic.not_an_argument_that_trivy_should_have_b: Nothing here characterises the record as wrong, spurious or a defect in Trivy. The dataset judges no finding (AAP 0.3.2). The record is unattributable to a package under this dataset's coordinate rules, and that is a statement about attribution, not about the tool.

adapters_carrying_this_condition.evidence: Those two modules are the only ones referencing paths.REJECT_UNFORMABLE_PACKAGE_COORDINATE; paths.py defines the constant and belongs to neither side of the count.
adapters_carrying_this_condition.arithmetic: Six adapter modules exist. Five are native, and of those five two are dependency-oriented -- trivy and dependency_check -- so the other three native adapters are the three named above. The sixth module, the shared adapters/sarif.py, is not dependency-oriented either: a SARIF result names a code location rather than a package, so package_coordinate is null on every SARIF row and its absence is never a rejection.
adapters_carrying_this_condition.seventh_adapter: adapters/osv_scanner.py would be dependency-oriented and would carry this condition, but AAP 0.6.1 makes it conditional on OSV-Scanner writing an artifact and it wrote none -- exit 128 with a stated no-work reason. The directory holds six modules and no osv_scanner.py, so the condition has exactly two carriers in this run.
adapters_carrying_this_condition.why_the_count_matters: It bounds where this rejection can legitimately appear. A rejection under this class from any of the other four adapters would be a defect in that adapter rather than a property of its artifact, and stating the boundary is what makes that checkable.

package_coordinate_precedence.authority: AAP 0.5.4's shared candidate precedence, implemented once in adapters/trivy.py's _package_coordinate and read there rather than restated from memory.

levels.candidate: a package URL on the record itself -- for Trivy, PkgIdentifier.PURL
a package URL on the enclosing package object -- an entry of Results[].Packages matched to the record by exact equality, read through Identifier.PURL or PkgIdentifier.PURL
<ecosystem>:<name>@<version> from the record's own fields -- the lower-cased enclosing Results[].Type, PkgName and InstalledVersion
the same ecosystem coordinate from the enclosing package's Name and Version

package_coordinate_precedence.the_two_trivy_routes: The tool's row in AAP 0.5.4 names two: PkgIdentifier.PURL, and PkgName plus InstalledVersion rendered <ecosystem>:<name>@<version>. Both appear -- the PURL route on rows 4, 5 and 6, and the ecosystem route on row 7 -- and they sit at three different precedence levels, because a PURL read from the enclosing package object is level 2 while a PURL read from the record is level 1. Reading the tool's two routes as two levels is the mistake row 5 catches: its coordinate is pkg:npm/handlebars@4.5.3, not npm:handlebars@4.5.3.
package_coordinate_precedence.ecosystem_is_lower_cased: _ecosystem_coordinate lower-cases the ecosystem before rendering. The one record that reaches level 3 states Type "bundler", which is already lower case, so this fixture asserts the shape and the separator placement -- <ecosystem> then a colon, <name> then an @, then <version> -- rather than an observable case change. Stated plainly because an assertion that a value did not change is weak evidence that it would have been changed, and pretending otherwise would overclaim what these rows prove.
package_coordinate_precedence.lexicographic_tiebreak_not_exercised: Where several candidates sit at one level the lexicographically smallest wins, implemented as sorted()[0] over the candidate set at levels 2 and 4. This fixture does not exercise it: the one record reaching level 2 matches exactly one Packages[] entry, and that entry states exactly one PURL, so the candidate set has one member and no tie arises. No winner is stated because there is no contest to state one for.
package_coordinate_precedence.no_coordinate_is_fabricated: Not from the Target, not from ArtifactName, not from the VulnerabilityID, and not from the PrimaryURL or DataSource the defective record does carry. The record names "nodejs-debug" in its Title and cve-2017-16137 in its PrimaryURL, and a plausible-looking pkg:npm/debug coordinate could be assembled from either -- the positive sibling's row 8 even carries pkg:npm/debug@2.6.8, from the PkgIdentifier this fixture removed. Assembling one here would be inference of exactly the kind AAP 0.5.4 forbids, it would make the rejection unreachable, and it would put a package version in the dataset that this artifact never stated. The field is not filled; the record is rejected and counted.

rejection_boundary.statement: An absent package coordinate on a dependency-oriented record is a rejection. The same absence on a record that is not dependency-oriented is a kept row with package_coordinate null. Nothing about the field distinguishes the two cases -- only the enclosing section array does.
rejection_boundary.why_it_can_only_be_a_rejection_here: The record is an element of Results[4].Vulnerabilities[], and adapters/trivy.py's _DEPENDENCY_ORIENTED_SECTIONS is frozenset({"Vulnerabilities"}). A vulnerability is a finding about a package; a vulnerability naming no package cannot be attributed to one with certainty, and AAP 0.5.4's rule for a record that cannot be attributed with certainty is to reject it and count the rejection under a named class -- never to guess a field. The two alternatives both hide it: dropping the record breaks raw finding records = dataset rows + rejected records, and inventing a coordinate puts a package this artifact never named into the dataset.
rejection_boundary.why_it_is_not_the_path_rejection_it_coul: The defective record's Target is a real file in the tree and resolves cleanly, so unresolvable_path and absent_path are both out. Its rule identifier and message are both present, so missing_rule_id and missing_message are out. It is a JSON object read from a supported section, so malformed_record and unattributable_section are out. It states no line at all, and absence is never a rejection, so non_integer_start_line is out. The classification order reaches the coordinate last precisely so that a record surviving the six earlier steps can only be rejected for the seventh, and this record survives all six.

mandatory_contrast_rows.also_contrast: Rows 1 and 3 are the same two cases again -- the second misconfiguration and the second secret -- so four of the eight rows carry a null coordinate and none of the four is rejected. Two are named above because two sections have to be represented; the other two are the same assertion repeated, and package_coordinate_absent counting 4 is where all four are visible at once.
mandatory_contrast_rows.why_these_rows_earn_their_place: Without them a fixture whose only null coordinate is the rejected one cannot tell a correct implementation from an over-eager one. An implementation that rejected every record with no formable coordinate, ignoring the section, would reject exactly the record this fixture is about and would satisfy every assertion an isolated defective record could carry -- while silently discarding every secret and every misconfiguration row Trivy ever produces. That is not a small loss: for this run's own artifact it is the entire dataset contribution, since all three of harness/artifacts/raw/trivy.json's records are misconfigurations and not one of them can form a package coordinate. The contrast rows are what make the section-dependence falsifiable, and they are why the fixture carries eight survivors rather than one.
mandatory_contrast_rows.how_to_break_it_deliberately: Add "Secrets" or "Misconfigurations" to _DEPENDENCY_ORIENTED_SECTIONS and re-run. Rows 0 to 3 must turn into rejections and rows 8, 4 and 4 must become 4, 8 and 5 -- if the suite still passes, the section-dependence is not being asserted anywhere and this block is the only thing that would have caught it.

not_a_rejection.case: a package coordinate absent from a Secrets[] or Misconfigurations[] record
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with package_coordinate null, counted under package_coordinate_absent
not_a_rejection.evidence: Rows 0 to 3. The section is outside _DEPENDENCY_ORIENTED_SECTIONS, so the absence test is never applied to them.

not_a_rejection.case: a path resolving outside the twelve authoritative globs
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with in_scope false, counted under rows_out_of_scope
not_a_rejection.evidence: Rows 4 to 7, from dev/package-lock.json and docs/Gemfile.lock. Both are real files in the pinned tree, 2168 and 89 lines. A runner legitimately reaching a manifest outside the twelve roots produces a kept row; out of scope means kept and marked, never rejected.

not_a_rejection.case: a start_line absent from every vulnerability record
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with start_line null, counted under start_line_absent
not_a_rejection.evidence: Rows 4 to 7, and the rejected record too -- its absence is counted at step 6, before step 7 rejects it for another reason entirely. An implementation reading absent as invalid would discard every Trivy vulnerability row.

not_a_rejection.case: a Results[] element holding no finding record at all
not_a_rejection.expected: no row, no rejection, counted under results_without_supported_section
not_a_rejection.evidence: /Results/5, whose Vulnerabilities array is present and empty. A scanned target with nothing to report is ordinary; there is no record to keep and none to reject.

rejection_boundary.defective_record_can_form_nothing_at_any: Verified from the fixture rather than assumed, level by level. Level 1: the record carries no PkgIdentifier member at all, so there is no record-level PURL. Level 2: the record carries no PkgID, no PkgName and no InstalledVersion, so _matching_packages returns an empty tuple before it inspects anything -- and /Results/4 carries no Packages array either, so there would have been nothing to match against had it tried. Level 3: PkgName and InstalledVersion are both absent, and _ecosystem_coordinate refuses to render a partial coordinate, so the enclosing Type "npm" cannot carry the level on its own. Level 4: no package matched, so there are no enclosing fields to read. All four fail for reasons stated in the artifact's own absences, and no reading of the record produces a fifth candidate.
rejection_boundary.no_guessed_coordinate: The rejected record is rejected and counted, never given a coordinate. Nothing in this file supplies one for it, not even a plausible one, and the positive sibling's pkg:npm/debug@2.6.8 is deliberately not carried across: it came from a PkgIdentifier this fixture does not contain.

counts.raw_count_unit: Results[] x one element of Vulnerabilities[], Secrets[] or Misconfigurations[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile._count_trivy walks independently of row construction, summing only the three supported sections
counts.raw_count_authority: normalize.reconcile.count_records("trivy", doc), whose traversal sums the length of each Results[] element's three supported sections and builds no row, resolves no path, maps no severity and forms no coordinate. It is the independent half of the identity: a count taken from the traversal that builds the rows would satisfy the assertion while testing nothing.
counts.rejections_by_class_completeness: One class, one member, and the other nine members of paths.REJECT_CLASSES are absent rather than present at zero -- absent_path, unresolvable_path, invalid_uri, ambiguous_source_resolution, missing_rule_id, missing_message, non_integer_start_line, unattributable_section and malformed_record. A test asserting the mapping equals {"unformable_package_coordinate": 1} therefore asserts both that the condition fired and that no other condition did, which a bare rejection count of 1 could not.
counts.row_order: Results[] in document order, the three sections in SUPPORTED_SECTIONS order within each element, and each section's elements in order. The rows below are in that order, and each row's index is its row_index under row_derivations. The rejected record would have been row 8; its removal shifts no other row, because it is last in document order.
counts.parse_status_authority: harness/lib/normalize/cli.py, PARSE_STATUS_PARTIAL = "partial", assigned as partial where there are rejections and clean where there are none. Partial is right precisely because the adapter did not abandon the artifact: every parsable record was emitted and the one rejected record is counted under its class, with its sub-reason retained. This is deliberately not normalize.reconcile's STATUS_PASS / STATUS_FAIL / STATUS_NOT_APPLICABLE vocabulary, which describes an assertion's outcome rather than an artifact's parse.

unsupported_finding_sections.state_in_this_fixture: present and empty on every one of the six Results[] elements
unsupported_finding_sections.expectation: validate_finding_sections returns None. An unsupported finding section that is present and empty satisfies "validated empty" and does not halt.
unsupported_finding_sections.why_this_matters_more_here: The halt runs over every element before a single row is built, so a non-empty Licenses or ExperimentalModifiedFindings would raise trivy.UnsupportedTrivySection and this fixture would never reach the record that carries its whole point. Recorded explicitly rather than by the silence of not mentioning it.
unsupported_finding_sections.not_to_be_blurred_with: The non-empty twin is oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/halt-trivy-unsupported-section.json, whose expected file records the exception. Nothing in this file expects a halt, and nothing in that one expects a row or a rejection.

results_holding_no_record.reading: Its Vulnerabilities array is present and empty, so it contributes no record and therefore neither a row nor a rejection. That is a scanned target with nothing to report, counted under results_without_supported_section. Two of the three lockfile Targets in this fixture do carry records -- dev/package-lock.json with two and docs/Gemfile.lock with two, four kept rows with in_scope false -- and this third one carries none; the distinction is the fixture's, not a dropped row.

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/trivy.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): twenty-three authored keys, then one records_* per supported section, one rows_class_* per scanner_class, one path_kind_* per normalize.paths.PATH_KINDS member and one severity_basis_* per normalize.severity.BASIS_VALUES member. The order above is that order, thirty-eight keys in total.
counters_note: Where the rejected record does and does not register is the whole of what separates these counters from the positive sibling's, and it is a consequence of the classification order rather than of anything about the record. It registers in exactly one counter: start_line_absent is 5, not 4, because step 6 records the absence before step 7 rejects it -- so five of the fixture's five vulnerability records state no line, four of them become rows and one does not. It registers in none of the others: records_vulnerabilities stays 5 because that counter is bumped per section length before any record is read, while package_coordinate_absent is 4 rather than 5 because that bump sits after the rejection returns, and every severity_*, path_kind_*, rows_class_*, rows_in_scope, rows_out_of_scope and multi_valued_* counter is reached only by a record that became a row. Four counters are simply the positive sibling's value minus one for the row that is now a rejection: rows_in_scope 4, rows_class_vuln 4, path_kind_tree_file 8 and severity_basis_label 8. Two more fall for reasons of their own: per_record_path_refinements is 0 because the PkgPath that produced the sibling's single refinement is one of the members this derivation removes, and severity_cvss_entries_present is 3 rather than 4 because the fourth CVSS table belongs to the rejected record and is never reached. Three are unchanged and worth reading anyway: known_non_finding_object_lists is 1 for the two-entry Packages inventory on /Results/2, which is what makes row 5's coordinate come from the enclosing-package level; results_without_supported_section is 1 for the empty-sectioned sixth element; and severity_cvss_entries_present 3 against severity_basis_cvss_score 0 is the label-over-score precedence made checkable -- three records carried scores and none of the three was consulted.

aap_reported_counters.note: The four counters AAP 0.5.4 has reported per tool. multi_location_records is 0 because no misconfiguration here carries a CauseMetadata.Occurrences array and a vulnerability and a secret each name exactly one location. multi_valued_cwe_records is 1: row 4's record lists CWE-1333 before CWE-400, so producer order disagrees with the ascending-numeric rule and the emitted value is CWE-400. The two alternatives each hide it: dropping the record breaks raw finding records = dataset rows + rejected records, and forming a coordinate from the Target, the ArtifactName, the VulnerabilityID or the PrimaryURL would put a package into the dataset that this artifact never named.
